newsitem.title: CHINA: China could delay some import tariffs - paper.
newsitem.headline: China could delay some import tariffs - paper.

text.p: China could delay the end of tariff exemptions on some imports of capital goods and raw materials for foreign ventures in an effort to avoid stunting economic growth, China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The State Council, or cabinet, was considering extending tariff-free grace periods to reassure foreign investors, the newspaper quoted an official of the General Tariff Administration of Customs as saying.

Beijing in April ended tariff exemptions on machinery and raw materials for foreign firms, but allowed foreign projects approved before the policy change to continue to enjoy the tariff-free treatment for a limited time, the newspaper said.
Foreign-funded projects worth up to $30 million were exempt to the end of 1996 and projects worth over $30 million had until the end of 1997 before the preferential treatment ended.
"It is not totally impossible for the state to reconsider the length of that grace period," the official said but gave to details.
Customs authorities had taken in 47.4 billion yuan in import duties from January to July, up 27.4 percent from the same period a year ago, the official said.
